correctness.rationale: For all integers n>=3 and p>=0 the explicit powered-distance block matrix is exact. The 2n-dimensional orthogonal decomposition consists of constant, side-antisymmetric, paired-equal and paired-opposite modes with multiplicities 1,1,n-1,n-1. On the zero-sum hyperplane the scalar signs prove every regime and equality case; h(p)=3^p/(2^p-1) is strictly decreasing on (0,1] and h(1)=3. Centered Gram positive semidefiniteness and rank establish the full Hilbert statement. The real analytic implicit function theorem proves the order-(n-1)^-2 matching-deletion gain. 178 supplemental numerical assertions passed, but are not the proof.

value.rationale: The crown family is the standard distance-transitive graph formed by deleting a perfect matching from balanced complete bipartite graphs, a natural perturbation of an established exact negative-type case. The result classifies all n, shows the sharp loss of 1-negative type beyond n=4, determines critical affine dimensions and every nullspace, and quantifies the small positive gain over K_{n,n} to the second asymptotic order. These are motivated exact invariants, not arbitrary finite table entries.
